key_insight: ImageNet pretraining improved vocal fold boundary accuracy in both transformer-based pipelines, with roughly fourfold greater gains for Swin-UNet than TransUNet.
engineering_relevance: Automated vocal fold segmentation could reduce manual processing of intraglottal PIV images used to quantify tissue motion and phonatory flow.
method: Benchmarked UNet, UNet++, TransUNet, and Swin-UNet.
Compared transformer-based models trained from scratch versus ImageNet-pretrained weights.
Evaluated six pipelines across five seeds using overlap and boundary metrics.
evidence_signal: Using 16,344 expert-annotated images from 227 ex vivo canine phonation trials, evaluation on 50 held-out trials found mean Dice scores of 0.9734–0.9764, with boundary differences assessed using Holm-corrected trial-level Wilcoxon tests.
watch_item: Generalization beyond ex vivo canine images and the studied optical conditions remains unestablished.
paper_title: Effects of Deep Learning Architecture and Pretraining on Automated Vocal Fold Segmentation in Ex Vivo High-Speed Phonation Images
